title: Solid-State Batteries: Current State of Play

blocks.text: Prepared: 2026-11-05 · Scope: public sources dated January to October 2026

items: All-solid-state batteries remain in pilot and validation; disclosed funding exceeded US$1.3 billion across 57+ deals from 2025 to 1Q26 [1].
Semi-solid-state cells are already produced at GWh scale in China, while all-solid-state cells are not yet in mass production [1].
QuantumScape opened its Eagle Line pilot in San Jose on 2026-02-04 and reports core tool uptime above 90% [2][3].
Stated mass-production targets cluster around 2027 to 2028 (Samsung SDI, Toyota, BYD), but Toyota's date has slipped repeatedly [4].
Sulfide cells currently cost 2 to 3 times liquid lithium-ion cells, and one analysis expects the first commercial window to slip to 2030-2035 [5].

blocks.text: TrendForce describes the industry as in a critical phase of engineering validation and key technology breakthroughs. Development centers on sulfide-based and polymer/oxide composite electrolytes. Toyota, Honda, Nissan, and Samsung SDI are slightly ahead in small-scale pilot production, with 2026 focused on yield and quality [1].

In China, CATL, GAC, Geely, and BYD began tendering for pilot-production equipment in the second half of 2025. Major automakers are expected to start vehicle-level all-solid-state testing in 2026 [1].

QuantumScape inaugurated its highly automated Eagle Line on 2026-02-04, built around its Cobra separator process, to supply sampling cells to automakers and to let licensing partners demonstrate GWh-scale manufacturing [2]. In its Q2 2026 letter it reported customer samples shipping, volumes ramping, and a plan to double cell output again in 2H 2026. Partners include Volkswagen PowerCo and Honda (agreement announced 2026-06-18). Its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance is $250M to $275M [3].

Samsung SDI targets mass production in the second half of 2027 at Ulsan, though production has not started. Toyota targets 2027-2028 and began building an electrolyte plant with Idemitsu Kosan in January 2026. BYD shows a 480 Wh/kg sulfide cell and plans small-batch installations in 2027. CATL has disclosed no mass-production date [4].

Sulfide electrolytes have poor chemical stability and need inert or oxygen-free processing. SMM cites interface-impedance degradation (capacity retention below 90% after 1,000 cycles) and capacity loss of over 30% below -20 degrees C. It puts current sulfide cell costs at 2 to 3 times liquid lithium-ion, with cost relief depending on kiloton-scale electrolyte output planned for 2027 [5].

Automotive-grade validation needs 2 to 3 years of safety and reliability testing, and SMM expects large-scale vehicle launches only after 2028 [5]. Timelines have slipped before: Toyota's target moved from 2020 to 2023 to 2026 and now 2027-2028 [4]. NIO's semi-solid pack, launched in 2024, was discontinued after a few hundred units [4].

SMM forecasts 13.5 GWh of all-solid-state and 160 GWh of semi-solid-state shipments by 2028, with all-solid-state reaching about 4% penetration by 2030 and solid-state overall up to about 10% by 2035 [5]. These are one analyst's projections and should be treated as indicative.

items: Expect semi-solid cells in niche vehicles first, and all-solid-state in small volumes from about 2027-2028.
Treat announced dates skeptically; the pattern so far is slippage, and cost parity is not near.
Watch pilot-line yield, uptime, and automaker validation results rather than announcements alone.
